habitat: Solitary in dense bush or thickets, especially along watercourses and in parks and gardens. It may come out to fruiting shrubs.
summary: A fairly common summer visitor. A plain warbler with no distinctive markings or eye stripe, a stubby bill, a pink inner mouth, large dark eyes and a plump body. It is usually located by a quiet monotonous warbling song. Newman does not name the months. The Kemp name Garden Warbler and the code NB were left unchanged.

bill.shape: Rather stubby. The inner mouth is pink.

head.pattern: Plain, with no eye stripe. The eyes are large and dark.

viewNotes.note: Plain, plump, with a stubby bill and no eye stripe.
Large dark eyes. No colours are named.
The underside in flight is not described.

calls.description: A quiet, monotonous warbling from inside a bush, louder on arrival and before departure. No grade A recording from South Africa was found. The selected file is a grade A song from France. The filename is XC904341-05-09-2024_11h8_fauvette-des-jardins.wav.
